answer: In an agent-run farm economy, each agent buying nectar, tending a vine, or tracking a falcon must lock a separate bond to bid for jobs. The registry gives each bond one bidding slot, so splitting into fake identities creates no extra slots without extra capital. Bonds stay locked through a dispute window and are slashed for signing conflicting delivery receipts for the same job. An attacker must fund every identity and risks losing each bond used to cheat.
